newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio de Janeiro wants FBI office.
newsitem.headline: Rio de Janeiro wants FBI office.

text.p: The mayor of Rio de Janeiro has asked U.S. authorities to open a planned FBI office in Brazil in his city, rather than at the embassy in Brasilia, a spokesman for the mayor's office said on Thursday.
He said Mayor Luiz Paulo Conde had sent a letter with his request to the U.S. consul in Rio de Janeiro, citing the city's location and concerns over drug trafficking as the main reasons.
"The control and repression of drug trafficking are activities of international character and demand the integration of the police forces of this continent," Conde's letter said.
Drug trafficking has mushroomed in Rio's shantytowns in the past 10 years and has led to increased armed confrontation between traffickers and police as well as between rival gangs.

Brazil has become a major trans-shipment route for drugs from Latin America to the United States and Europe since crackdowns on drug smuggling in Brazil's neighbouring countries forced traffickers to reroute their operations.

A spokesman for the U.S. Consulate in Rio said there were plans to open an FBI office in the U.S. Embassy compound in Brasilia in 1997 or 1998, but he would not say whether Rio might be an alternative location.
He said the FBI office would have three staff members and collaborate with Brazilian authorities by exchanging information in areas of mutual interest and by training Brazilian police officers.
Funding for the FBI office still has to be approved and the Brazilian government has to give its consent, the consular spokesman said.
The FBI has one office in South America, in Montevideo, Uruguay.
